_about.what: HAND-AUTHORED, and the only file under docs/ that is. Raven's per-monster part review: the name a parts row carries, the name each dropdown item carries, and which item the row opens on.
_about.written_by: NOTHING. No script writes this file and none ever should. Its four neighbours are all generated and WILL overwrite whatever is put in them -- partnames.json by build-part-names.py, part-rest.json by build-partrest.py, part-states.json by build-partstates.py, monsters.json by harvest-monsters.py. buildlib.write_json_atomic refuses this basename so a future script cannot take it by accident.
_about.meaning: An entry here means one thing: a human looked at this row against the render. That is why it is not seeded from partnames.json -- a seeded name could not be told from a typed one.
_about.rowKeys: monster id -> rows -> the row's part-id set, exactly as clusterGroups() joins it: numeric order, comma, no spaces. The same key partnames.json uses, so the two line up row for row.
_about.optionKeys: an option's ON-set -- the ids printed after 'on' in the label, with the rage ladder's own parts stripped as groupLabelWithout strips them. 'none' for the all-off option. NEVER a group index: those are invisible in the UI, and a ladder choice's rep is just its first member. Verified unique per row across all 540 multi-member rows in the library.
_about.resolution: exact ON-set match first, then a UNIQUE containment fallback. 0 or 2+ matches warns and resolves to nothing. Exact-first is load-bearing: em001_04 row 8,11,12,101 has options 11,101 / 12,101 / 8, so the bare key '101' is ambiguous and must be rejected rather than silently first-matched.
_about.reach: A ROW DEFAULT REACHES ONLY RENDERED ROWS. The panel drops inert single-member rows and ladder rows that collapse to one choice, so parts living in those are still DEFAULT_PARTS_OFF / DEFAULT_PARTS_ON's business in render/monster.js. Those tables also feed stateParts() and the test that decides whether the Enraged checkbox appears at all, which nothing here can express.
_about.order: Dropdown order is the ROM's own member order unless a row carries an explicit `order` array of option keys, which then leads and unlisted options follow in ROM position. It has to be an ARRAY: the `options` object cannot carry order, because JS iterates integer-like keys ascending, so {"9":..,"1":..} comes back 1 then 9. Used where the ROM's order puts the damaged state above the healthy one -- Rathian's eye row reads 'Closed / Open' without it.
_about.rage: A monster entry may carry a `rage` map naming the Rage dropdown's rungs, keyed by that select's own value: 0 is No Rage, 1..n the rungs in order. rageLadder() otherwise reads them off the clip names, which gives 'Level 1' / 'Max' -- true to the ROM and meaningless to a player. Anything unnamed keeps the generated label. It may also carry a "name", which RELABELS THE CONTROL ITSELF -- rageLadder() calls every ladder Rage because that is what a ladder usually is, and on Boltreaver the rungs come out Green and Cyan, its charge colours rather than a temper. Rung keys are all integers so "name" cannot collide with one. **A RUNG NAMED null IS NOT OFFERED:** "0": null drops the No Rage rung, for a monster that is never in that state, and the current level moves to the lowest rung that remains. Any rung may go, not only the zeroth; dropping every rung warns and keeps them all.
_about.names: A `name` or an `options` entry means A PERSON TYPED IT while looking at the render -- that is what the row tooltip says, and what suppresses the community join's low/ambiguous/shared flags. So a MIGRATION from DEFAULT_PARTS_ON / DEFAULT_PARTS_OFF carries `default` ONLY: the default was already Raven's call, the names were not. Until he names them the row keeps its community name and its flags, which is the honest state.
_about.mergedRows: A row key joining several row keys with '+' replaces those rows with ONE control, and each of its options names one member per source row, joined the same way: "8,9+10,11": {options: {"8+10":"Intact", "9+10":"Cracked", "9+11":"Broken"}}. Both source clusters are still applied, one member each, exactly as two separate rows would -- this is presentation and nothing else. Refused, with a warning, if a source is a rage-ladder row: there the members are variants the Rage control picks between, and merging would take that decision away from it.
_about.reviewedRowsAlwaysShow: Naming a row makes the panel SHOW it, and makes the parts in its option keys the user's choice rather than the Rage control's. The panel normally folds away a cluster whose members differ only in what rage decides -- right for a rage aura, wrong for Tigrex's right front leg, where ROM_RAGE_SET happens to name parts 8 and 10 that are really a break state. This does not overrule the ROM about what rage DOES; the rage sets still apply. It changes only whether the row is offered.
_about.perStateOptionKeys: An option key written 'calmKey|rageKey' is ONE item with two forms: it resolves to whichever half the current state wants, and the other half is removed from the list so it is not offered as a third choice. Akantor's back row is the case -- 7, 8 and 8,9 are two states not three, 8 being the broken back and 8,9 the same break plus part 9, the layer its enraged form adds. Distinct from the row-level `rage` key, which chooses a different DEFAULT: here the choice does not move, only what it draws.
_about.rowOrder: A monster entry may carry a `rowOrder` array of row keys, which sets the order the Parts panel lists them in; anything it does not name keeps its cluster position after the ones it does. The panel otherwise follows the ROM's cluster order -- the order the parts table happens to be authored in, which put Ukanlos' eyes at the bottom under its tail.
_about.hiddenRows: A row may carry "hidden": true. Its default -- and its per-state `rage` default -- still apply, exactly as a visible row's would; it is simply not offered in the panel. For a consequence of the rage state rather than a choice anyone makes, like Gypceros' enraged eye glow.
_about.mergedOptionKeys: A merged row's option key names ONLY the source rows that are ON -- "11,13,15" style, written '+'-joined as "11+13+15" -- and every source it does not name falls to that source's own all-off option. Each half is matched by its ON-SET, which is unique to one source, so the older positional form ("8+10", "102+103", "2+3") resolves identically. Written this way because Congalala's Item row merges NINE clusters and a positional key would be eight ninths 'none'.
_about.hideOption: A row may carry a `hide` array of option keys to drop from the list. For an option the row really has but which cannot be offered yet -- Blangonga's second eye mesh, where two parts both carry XfB_0__m00_eye and what reaches the second is unread. Distinct from a 'calm|rage' half, which is hidden because the other state owns it; this is hidden because nobody knows what it is. Deleting the key restores it.
_about.view: A monster entry may carry "view": {"list": "0", "clip": "Motion[2]_loop"} -- the motion list and clip the viewer opens that monster on, where the ROM's first list and first clip are not the one worth landing on. Moved here from a DEFAULT_VIEW constant in index.html 2026-09-11: these are Raven's calls made while reviewing a monster, the same kind of judgement as a part name, so one monster is one entry in one file. The clip is only honoured when its list is the one showing, so a mismatched pair cannot drop the monster onto a clip from the wrong list.
_about.stateAxis: A row may carry "state": "charged" or "heated" to make its "off|on" option keys split on that control instead of Rage; its per-state default key is then `charged` or `heated`. Charged is mutually exclusive with Rage (see matState()); HEATED is independent of both, being an armour state rather than an AI one, and defaults ON. The Heated control exists ONLY where a review row asks for it -- nothing in the ROM marks the state, only the lava materials on the meshes, and reading 'has a lav* material' as 'has a heated state' would be an inference. Lagiacrus' Shocker is the charged case, Agnaktor the heated one. A MERGED row's option key may also be per-state, split on '|' before '+' -- "calmHalves|enragedHalves" -- so the whole combination swaps. Najarala's back needs that: calm draws crest 103 alone, enraged draws 103 with its alpha layer 113 AND the body's own 8, 9 from the other source row. Declaring "state": "rage" on a row also OFFERS the Enraged control, the same way "charged" and "heated" do, for a monster the ROM gives no other sign of having one. A row may also carry "state": "level", which splits on the monster's LEVEL AXIS instead of a boolean: the axis value is the rung index, so a key carries one half per rung. And it may carry "state": {"on": "<part ids>"} to split on ANOTHER ROW -- true whenever every part named is currently drawn. Nargacuga's eyes use that: Closed is "5,6|5", both lids normally and one lid when the broken-head mesh (part 2) is on. Keyed on the PART rather than the watched row's option so it cannot depend on panel order -- state.groups is written before any row is built -- and so it survives the watched row being renamed, reordered or merged. A pick on a monster with a watcher rebuilds the whole panel.
_about.levels: A monster entry may carry "levels": {"name": "Charge", "rungs": [...]} -- a control with MORE THAN TWO values, which none of the three checkboxes can express. The rungs are named BY HAND because nothing in the ROM names them: Astalos' two charge materials carry one clip called 'Animation' and one with no name at all, which is why rageLadder() -- which reads rungs off level tokens in clip names -- finds nothing and that monster had no state control of any kind. The control appears only where some row says "state": "level", the same way Heated appears only where a row asks for it. Rung 0 is the default. A key on a level row carries one half per rung and is CLAMPED to its last half when short, so a two-step axis on a three-rung control is written "a|b" -- or spelled out, as Astalos' eyes are: "2|2|52", part 2 through Uncharged and Charging and part 52 at Fully Charged.
_about.variants: A monster entry may carry "variants": {"name": "Gender", "options": [{"name": "Female", "off": "4,5,6"}, ...]} -- a control picking between WHOLE ALTERNATIVE BODIES that share one part table. Each option's `off` names the parts to force off, applied AFTER partsDrawn builds the map, because no option and no DEFAULT_PARTS_OFF entry can reach them: every member of the cluster draws the body, and leaving a cluster with no member on makes applyParts draw all of it. A row may say "variant": N to belong to one option alone, and is then offered only while that body is on screen. **THIS IS A VIEWER CONSTRUCT, not a decode.** Kelbi is the case -- two complete Kelbis in one model, 966 and 992 vertices, drawn on top of each other because it has no defaultSet and no rest sets at all. The game certainly picks one and this project has not read where; the part table holds no notion of gender. Names come from the render.

Kelbi has **no part 0** -- no shared body at all -- just two clusters, and **parts 1 and 4 are COMPLETE BODIES**, 966 and 992 vertices, with the male half again as wide (11015 against 6516, on heights of 16741 and 16643). Parts 2/3 and 5/6 are that body's small and large horns, and the male pair is much the taller (6 is 9135 high against 3's 2841), which is the size difference he saw. Every cluster always has exactly one member on, so **the panel drew 1, 3, 4 and 6 -- both bodies and both sets of large horns, one inside the other.** 101 and 104 are proxy-only and never drew. **NOTHING THAT EXISTED COULD FIX IT:** an option can only choose a member and every member of the male cluster draws part 4; DEFAULT_PARTS_OFF gives up by its own rule that a cluster with no alternative turning the part off is left alone; and leaving a cluster with NO member on is worse, because partsDrawn only lists parts an on-group mentions and applyParts draws anything it does not hear about. So a new capability was added -- a per-monster `variants` control that forces parts off AFTER the drawn map is built, plus a per-row `variant` key so a row is offered only while its body is on screen. **THE ROM PICKS A GENDER SOMEWHERE AND WE HAVE NOT DECODED IT, and that is why this control is honest only as a viewer construct.** Kelbi has NO defaultSet and NO rest sets whatever -- part-rest.json holds nothing for ems003_00 -- so the panel fell to the highest index in each cluster and drew both. The part table contains no notion of gender; it holds two clusters the viewer happened to draw together. 'Gender', 'Female' and 'Male' are read off the render by Raven and off the geometry by me, NOT off the ROM, and the selection the game really makes is still unread. Horn names are small/large in ROM member order, which is the order he read them in. **NO EYE PARTS, AND NONE ARE HIDDEN.** Raven: 'I don't see the eye parts, they may be turned off.' They are not -- **the whole model is 8 meshes carrying ONE material, XfBA1__m00_body**, so there is no eye geometry to turn off and nothing the Gender control could be suppressing. Kelbi's eyes are painted into the body texture. Checked across the small monsters and **this is the normal case, not a Kelbi defect: only 3 of 24 sampled have an eye material at all** -- Felyne and Melynx (XfB_0__m01_eye plus a second XfB_0__m02_eye_yoi) and Conga (XfB_0__m00_eye). Every other small monster checked, Aptonoth, Bullfango and Anteka included, has none. The 1xx parts are not candidates either: 101 and 104 are proxy-only and measure 6420x17927x30042 and 10696x20605x32693, body-sized cut-solid shells for bodies 1 and 4 rather than anything facial.
